note: All 24 expected values below were hand-derived from the frozen specification (PROJECT_BOOK §9) and the hand-written fixtures. They were NOT copied from any program output. finalState lists the key terminal fields only (message/tool-call order, shared state, pending calls, run status); canonical hashes are computed by the Oracle at run time and are not hand-derivable.

G01.rationale: AG-UI #1524: the checkpoint after index 4 already contains closed call-1; FULL_REPLAY re-applies TOOL_CALL_START at index 2 over it, so the resume path holds call-1 twice. The DUPLICATE_TOOL_CALL diagnostic carries sourceIndex 2 (the replayed START itself), but the first divergence under PROJECT_BOOK §8.6 is the first comparable state difference: the sliced step comparison starts at the checkpoint (index 4), where the full path holds one call-1 and the resume path already holds two — so firstDivergenceSourceIndex is 4. Steps below the checkpoint are not comparable (the resume state there is the checkpoint base itself); an unsliced comparison would report an artefact at index 0. Diagnostic sourceIndex (2) and first state-divergence sourceIndex (4) are two different values and must not be conflated (FIX-R1, P1-R1-01).

G02.rationale: AG-UI #3119: the checkpoint snapshot at index 7 re-ID'd msg-a to msg-a2 and the reconciliation appended the new id at the end, so the tool result message now precedes its assistant message (full order assistant-then-tool, resume tool-then-assistant). The divergence already exists at the checkpoint restore (index 7).

G03.rationale: AG-UI #3368: full path keeps msg-1 as two segments ('Hello, ' / 'it is sunny.') with the tool call between them in the timeline; the checkpoint snapshot at index 10 merged them into one string, so the second half is displayed as part of the first block before the tool call. Message ids match, but the interleave is lost, hence MESSAGE_REORDER at the checkpoint restore (index 10). Shortest reproduction: remapping the assistant id in the checkpoint also breaks its order against the tool result.

G04.rationale: The resume stream drops TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT 'world' (index 3), so resume msg-1 holds only 'Hello ' while full holds 'Hello world'. First divergence is the dropped event itself (index 3).

G05.rationale: Adjacent TOOL_CALL_ARGS fragments at indices 4 and 5 are swapped, so resume args read '"x"}{"q":' instead of '{"q":"x"}'. The two paths first disagree at index 4, where the full path has applied '{"q":' and the resume path has applied '"x"}'.

G06.rationale: Recovery uses the snapshot at index 1 (counter 1) although the disconnect point is index 3, discarding the deltas at 2 and 3; resume shared state stays {counter 1} while full reaches {counter 2}. First divergence is index 2, the first discarded delta.

G07.rationale: No stable event id exists (all sourceEventKeys null), so the replayed TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT 'Hello' (index 2) cannot be de-duplicated: it is applied a second time and resume msg-1 reads 'HelloHello'. Per §4.3 this is SUSPECTED_DUPLICATE, not an automatic dedup; the doubled content makes the verdict INCONSISTENT.

G08.rationale: The stream ends at index 4 with the tool call still open and no RUN_FINISHED/RUN_ERROR, so the run is truncated (verdict INCOMPLETE_TRACE, warning TRUNCATED_RUN). The resume path additionally lacks the args at index 4, the first index where the two paths disagree. No injection is needed to reproduce this: the trace itself is truncated, so the shortest sequence is empty.

N01.rationale: Single normal text run; the checkpoint after index 2 covers the run start and the first content, and the remaining END/FINISHED apply cleanly, so both paths converge. Dropping the first resume event (TEXT_MESSAGE_END) is the shortest breakage.

N02.rationale: Three content segments concatenate in arrival order to 'Hello brave world.' on both paths; the checkpoint after index 3 preserves the first two segments.

N03.rationale: Normal tool call: START/ARGS/END before the checkpoint, RESULT and the closing text after it; one call, one result, both paths agree.

N04.rationale: Frontend tool call: run-1 ends successfully with pendingToolCallIds [call-1] (no same-run result is required, §3.14); run-2 returns the result, which clears the pending entry. Both paths end with no pending calls.

N05.rationale: STATE_SNAPSHOT replaces shared state, then two STATE_DELTAs apply in order (replace count to 3, add items); the checkpoint after the snapshot plus the remaining deltas reproduces the same state.

N06.rationale: Full replay from the empty state applies the identical MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT (same id, same content, same position), so reconciliation rule 1 replaces msg-1 in place and both paths agree.

N07.rationale: Normal disconnect: the complete checkpoint after index 4 covers the message prefix ('Hello ') and the shared-state snapshot, and the remaining content/end apply cleanly.

N08.rationale: Same messageId legally reopened (same role, no tool call between the segments), so the timeline is preserved and both paths hold 'Hello, world.' in two segments. Unlike G03, no tool call intervenes and nothing is merged.

N09.rationale: Two independent tool calls interleave (START/START/ARGS/ARGS/END/END) and each receives exactly one result; the checkpoint after both ENDs plus the remaining results reproduces the same state.

N10.rationale: Two runs in one thread execute in order; the checkpoint after run-1 finishes and run-2 applies cleanly on top of it.

N11.rationale: RUN_ERROR may precede RUN_STARTED (§3.5, start failure); the following run starts normally and finishes, so the terminal state is FINISHED on both paths.

N12.rationale: RUN_ERROR ends the unfinished stream, so it is the terminal event: the message and tool call stay open/incomplete and runStatus is ERROR on both paths, with no fake TOOL_CALL_RESULT inferred.

N13.rationale: Timestamps decrease (1000, 900, 800, 700, 600) but arrival order is correct; timestamp must never reorder events (§3.1), so both paths fold in file order and agree.

N14.rationale: The two 'Hello' contents belong to different messageIds (msg-1, msg-2) and carry different stable sourceEventKeys (k-a, k-b), so they are distinct events and neither is a duplicate; both paths hold two messages.

N15.rationale: Identical args '{"q":"x"}' are used by two different toolCallIds; the calls are distinct, each gets its own result, and no duplicate is reported.

N16.rationale: The checkpoint covers only the shared state (count 5); message coverage is false, so the local message msg-1 ('Local text') is kept from the prefix fold instead of being wiped, and both paths agree.
